name: Lemon Garlic Chicken with Sauteed Spinach
instructions: Season chicken with salt, pepper, and lemon zest.
Heat olive oil in a skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken 6 mins per side until golden and cooked through.
Add minced garlic, cook 1 min until fragrant.
Squeeze lemon juice over chicken, add spinach, wilt for 2 mins.
tips: Add red pepper flakes for a spicy kick.

name: Classic Tomato Basil Pasta
instructions: Cook pasta according to package instructions.
Dice tomatoes. Heat olive oil, sauté garlic for 1 min.
Add tomatoes, cook 8 mins until softened into a sauce.
Toss drained pasta with sauce, top with torn basil and parmesan.
tips: Use San Marzano tomatoes for the best flavor.

name: Paneer Butter Masala
instructions: Melt butter in a pan and sauté tomato puree until oil separates.
Add garam masala, chili powder, and salt to taste.
Stir in cream and half a cup of water to create a smooth gravy.
Add paneer cubes and simmer for 5 minutes.
Crush kasuri methi between palms and sprinkle over the curry before serving.
tips: Soak paneer in warm water for 10 minutes before cooking for a softer texture.

name: Vegetable Stir-Fry with Tofu
instructions: Press tofu to remove water, then cut into cubes and brown in a wok with oil.
Remove tofu; add ginger-garlic paste and vegetables to the hot wok.
Stir-fry on high heat for 4 minutes until crisp-tender.
Add soy sauce and tofu back into the wok.
Toss everything together and drizzle with sesame oil.
tips: Ensure the wok is smoking hot before adding veggies to maintain crunch.

name: Bhetki Macher Paturi
instructions: Marinate fish with mustard paste, turmeric, salt, and mustard oil for 30 mins.
Lightly singe banana leaves over a flame to make them flexible.
Place a fish fillet and one chili on a leaf, then fold into a neat parcel.
Tie with thread and steam or slow-cook on a flat griddle for 7 mins per side.
Serve hot with steamed Basmati rice.
tips: Use a mix of yellow and black mustard seeds for a balanced pungent kick.

name: Tawa Fish Fry
instructions: Make a paste of chili powder, turmeric, salt, and lemon juice.
Coat the fish steaks thoroughly and marinate for 20 minutes.
Heat coconut oil on a tawa (griddle) and add curry leaves.
Place fish on the tawa and fry for 5-6 minutes on each side until charred.
Garnish with fresh onion rings and lime wedges.
tips: Coconut oil is essential for the authentic coastal flavor profile.

name: Mushroom Risotto
instructions: Sauté onions and mushrooms in butter until soft.
Add Arborio rice and toast for 2 minutes until translucent at edges.
Add warm broth one ladle at a time, stirring constantly until absorbed.
Repeat until rice is creamy and 'al dente' (about 20 minutes).
Off the heat, vigorously stir in parmesan and a knob of cold butter.
tips: Never rinse the rice; the surface starch is what makes the risotto creamy.

name: Hyderabadi Bagara Baingan
instructions: Dry roast peanuts, sesame, and coconut; grind into a thick, smooth paste.
Slit eggplants crosswise (keeping stems attached) and deep fry until 70% cooked.
Heat oil, add tempering spices, then sauté the ground paste and ginger-garlic.
Add tamarind juice, salt, and water to create a thick gravy.
Stuff or drop the eggplants into the gravy and simmer until tender.
tips: Frying the eggplants before adding them to the gravy prevents them from getting mushy.

name: Chicken Hakka Noodles
instructions: Boil noodles 'al dente', drain, and toss with a drop of oil to prevent sticking.
Heat oil in a wok; stir-fry chicken strips on high heat until cooked.
Add shredded vegetables and chilies; toss for 2 minutes on high heat.
Add noodles, soy sauce, salt, pepper, and vinegar.
Toss vigorously for 3 minutes until well combined and slightly charred.
tips: Use a high-smoke point oil like canola or peanut oil for the best wok hei flavor.

name: Luchi with Alur Dom
instructions: Knead flour with ghee and water into a smooth dough; rest for 20 mins.
Boil and peel baby potatoes; prick them and lightly fry in mustard oil.
Make the gravy with ginger, tomato, hing, and cumin; simmer potatoes in it.
Roll out small discs from the dough and deep fry until they puff up.
Serve the fluffy Luchis hot with the spicy potato curry.
tips: Ensure the oil is very hot before dropping in the Luchi to ensure they puff perfectly.

name: Classic Greek Salad (Horiatiki)
instructions: Roughly chop cucumber and tomatoes into large chunks.
Thinly slice the red onion into half-moons.
Combine vegetables and olives in a bowl.
Place a whole block of feta on top or crumble it in large pieces.
Drizzle generously with olive oil and sprinkle with dried oregano.
tips: Authentic Greek salad never contains lettuce; use the highest quality [olive oil](https://www.greece-is.com) you can find.

name: Ven Pongal
instructions: Pressure cook rice and moong dal with 3 cups of water until very soft/mushy.
Heat ghee in a small pan; fry cashews until golden and set aside.
In the same ghee, crackle cumin, peppercorns, ginger, and curry leaves.
Pour this tempering over the cooked rice-dal mixture and mash slightly.
Mix in salt and the fried cashews before serving with coconut chutney.
tips: Lightly roasting the moong dal before cooking enhances the nutty aroma of the dish.

name: Prawn Malai Curry
instructions: Lightly fry the prawns with a pinch of turmeric and salt; set aside.
Heat mustard oil and temper with cardamom, cinnamon, and cloves.
Add ginger paste and sauté until the raw smell disappears.
Pour in the thick coconut milk and bring to a gentle simmer.
Add prawns and slit chilies; cook for 5 minutes until the gravy thickens.
tips: Do not overcook the prawns, or they will become rubbery in the creamy sauce.

name: Medhu Vada
instructions: Soak urad dal for 4 hours; grind into a thick, fluffy paste using minimal water.
Aerate the batter by whisking vigorously until it floats in water.
Mix in chopped ginger, chilies, peppercorns, and salt.
Wet your palms, shape batter into donuts, and slide into hot oil.
Deep fry until golden brown and crispy on the outside.
tips: The key to light vadas is incorporating air into the batter during the whisking stage.

name: Mapo Tofu
instructions: Toast and grind Sichuan peppercorns; set aside.
Sauté minced meat in a wok until browned; add doubanjiang and stir-fry.
Pour in stock and add cubed tofu very gently to avoid breaking.
Simmer for 5 minutes, then stir in cornstarch slurry to thicken.
Top with ground peppercorns and chopped scallions.
tips: Blanch the tofu in salted boiling water for 1 minute before using to help it hold its shape.

name: Chicken Saltimbocca
instructions: Place a slice of prosciutto and two sage leaves on each cutlet; secure with a toothpick.
Dredge only the bottom side of the chicken in flour.
Melt butter in a skillet and sear chicken (prosciutto side down first).
Flip and cook for 2 minutes; deglaze the pan with white wine.
Reduce wine by half to create a silky sauce and serve immediately.
tips: Use a dry Pinot Grigio or Sauvignon Blanc for the best sauce acidity.

name: Shakshuka
instructions: Sauté onions and bell peppers in a skillet until softened.
Add garlic, cumin, and paprika; pour in tomatoes and simmer for 10 minutes.
Make small wells in the sauce and crack an egg into each.
Cover and cook for 5-8 minutes until whites are set but yolks are runny.
Garnish with crumbled feta and fresh parsley.
tips: Serve with crusty bread or pita to soak up the spiced tomato sauce and egg yolks.
